question:
Work only in the provided graph. Two people share the name 'Gerhard Schröder':
  X = Q2530
  Y = Q60781
Determine whether X and Y are connected by FAMILY: a path in which EVERY hop uses one of the kinship properties P22 (father), P25 (mother), P26 (spouse), P40 (child), P3373 (sibling), in either direction. Sharing a name is not evidence of family, and edges() shows every property, not only these five — filtering is your job. A claim that no such path exists is only credible if you have exhausted the search, so report every entity in X's kinship component, X included.

answer.format: Call FINAL with exactly this JSON and no prose: {"connected":true|false,"x_component":["Q...", ...]} where x_component lists every entity reachable from X through kinship properties, X included.

certificate.true_absence: X's kinship component closes at 9 members without Y; Y's own component has 3 and the two are disjoint
certificate.temptation: X and Y are joined by a DIRECT edge ['P1889'] that is not a kinship property — every pathfinder returns it in one hop
certificate.proof_obligation: the answer is scored on the component, so a correct 'no' reached by stopping early fails

baseline.correct: returns the 1-hop non-kinship edge — a confident false positive
